done_when: A forge test run with no output for 10 minutes prints one plain line saying how long it has been silent and how to stop it, and the run is not killed

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a long-running silent test command.
The clock advances 600 times faster while the production watcher still polls once per real second. Every observation therefore occurs at least ten simulated minutes apart. Removing the ten-minute guard entirely would still pass all three cases and the spacing assertion, although production would print a reminder every second. The named proof consequently does not verify the initial threshold or repetition limit. Exercise observations less than ten simulated minutes apart and assert that notices remain absent before each deadline.
findings.title: Gate: test_1_silent_tests_report_the_wait_without_stopping

why: A forge test run can sit silent at 0% CPU with no sign that it is stuck (issue 1366)
